accounting.rationale: The paragraph mixes derived-type parameterization, structure terminology, intrinsic assignment/no intrinsic operations, constructor availability, admitted use contexts, and user-defined operations; each is accounted separately to avoid duplicating detailed owners.
Derived types can be parameterized. 7.5.3 and the type-parameter catalogues own parameter declaration, defaults, and value restrictions.

A scalar derived-type object is a structure, structure assignment is intrinsic, and derived types have no intrinsic operations. 7.5.1, 7.1.5, and 10.2.1.3 retain the actual operation and assignment plans.
Each derived type has a structure constructor for creating values. R756-R758 and C7101-C7111 plus 7.5.10 source plans own constructor syntax, restrictions, and value effects.

Objects of derived type can be used as procedure arguments and function results and can appear in I/O lists. Procedure association/result and I/O-list restrictions are owned by Clauses 12 and 15, not by this overview sentence.
Additional operations can be defined by procedures. Defined-operation and generic-resolution obligations are owned by 10.1.6 and Clause 15 catalogues.
Cross-reference only: detailed derived-type concepts are described in 7.5 and already registered in the derived_types_7_5_* catalogues.
